detail.problem: Shock part: the rule requires ALL five features at once (and SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30, (confusion or restlessness), weakness). The page's comma list is ambiguous, but the circulation box on the same page uses the same comma construction with an explicit 'or' ('If shock/SBP < 80, pulse >= 100 or heavy bleeding'), and clinically a patient with SBP < 80 and pulse >= 100 who is not weak or confused is still in shock. As written the probable shock diagnosis will almost never fire, so (active_condition Shock) in the priority rule is nearly dead; the Emergency level is still reached via the standalone SBP<80 and pulse>=100 criteria, so the triage consequence is limited, but the diagnosis is wrong in logic. Each concept choice is fine (Clouded consciousness / Acute confusion for confusion, Restlessness, Asthenia for weakness, RR > 30 bpm). Acute heart failure part: correctly expanded as (and Swelling of lower limb (or Orthopnea, Dyspnea on exertion)) inside the pulse<50 branch. Footnote 1 (palliative) and 2 (jaw-thrust) are management.

Footnote 3 lists SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30, confusion/restlessness, weakness as signs for 'shock likely'; the rule requires ALL of them (including weakness) simultaneously, so it will almost never fire. A 'consider' list is probably meant as any-of or a k-of-n. Also footnote 3 (leg swelling, difficulty breathing worse lying/with effort = acute heart failure) is encoded in the pulse<50 priority branch only; footnote 1 (life-limiting illness/CPR) is not logic.

Footnote 3a (acute heart failure = leg swelling + dyspnea worse lying down or with effort) is encoded correctly in the bradycardia branch. Footnote 3b (shock likely) is encoded as probable Shock = SBP<80 AND pulse≥100 AND RR>30 AND (Clouded consciousness OR Acute confusion OR Restlessness) AND Asthenia. All concepts are right, but requiring all five criteria makes the rule almost never fire (see rule-level problems). 'Clouded consciousness' is a looser match for 'confusion' than Acute confusion.
